claims.text: The targeted material family is fcc high-entropy alloys derived from Fe-Co-Ni, including CoCrFeMnNi and Co-rich variants.
The targeted mechanical property is improved strength-ductility synergy at cryogenic temperatures.
Optimization of saturation magnetization is an additional targeted property.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi forms a chemically disordered, single-phase fcc solid solution at ambient pressure.
Co40Fe25Cr20Ni15 is a Co-rich fcc variant of the targeted alloy family.
Fcc CoCrFeMnNi undergoes paramagnetic-to-spin-glass and spin-glass-to-ferromagnetic transitions at approximately 93 K and 38 K, respectively.
Cr moments align antiferromagnetically relative to the moments in their local coordination environment and thereby reduce the net magnetic moment.
Strong electronic hybridization contributes to cancellation of the Fe and Co moments.
The alloy has a high electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Chemical disorder, lattice distortion, and magnetic ordering make the orbital moment contribution difficult to isolate and enhance.
Cr-induced antiferromagnetic coupling suppresses both the net orbital moment and the net spin moment.
Lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch improves solid-solution strength in fcc HEAs.
Lattice distortion broadens the electronic density of states and complicates prediction of the orbital moment.
In fcc HEAs, Co and Cr decrease stacking-fault energy, whereas Fe and Ni increase it.
Compositionally balancing stacking-fault energy can promote mechanical twinning and improve strength-ductility synergy.
Co40Fe25Cr20Ni15 will exhibit enhanced cryogenic strength-ductility synergy because of deformation twinning.
The Cr-containing Co-rich alloy will have a lower net magnetic moment than a pure Fe-Co-Ni alloy because of persistent antiferromagnetic Cr alignment.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi has a room-temperature strength of about 410 MPa and elongation of about 50%.
The cited records do not define a Cr-content threshold at which antiferromagnetic coupling completely suppresses the orbital moment.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to single-phase fcc solid solutions and may not transfer to high-Al BCC or phase-separated multiphase alloys.
